exposure: Chest-to-head circumference ratio (<10th percentile, 10th-90th percentile, >90th percentile)
cohort: 83,822 non-anomalous singletons born at 34-41 weeks' gestation to mothers with no history of previous cesareans or uterine surgery
finding: A low chest-to-head circumference ratio at birth was associated with an increased rate of breech presentation and transverse lie.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was performed in 96.8% of breech presentations and 63.4% of transverse lie births.
